subject: Request: Completion-window waiver + safe-retry spec for nightly bulk jobs

Subject: Nightly bulk completion window - waiver request

Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited about Redwood's throughput, but one thing that will be a hard requirement for our finance batch is a relaxed completion window. Our nightly job processes 40M rows and occasionally runs long when third-party enrichment calls spike. Can we get a contract carveout that treats completion within a 6–12 hour window as compliant (instead of strict 2-hour completion)?

We'd also like clarity on retry behavior — we need "at-most-once" end results (no duplicate invoices) and guidance on idempotency keys, TTLs, and your recommended dedupe window. I've attached our internal batch SLA request form.

Appreciate any proposed wording we can include in the SOW.

—Elena

Thanks for the ping. Internal engineering notes / constraints below — high-level and operational (we can convert to client-friendly wording once you confirm):

1) Completion window carveout: we can treat a "grace window" up to 12 hours for the nightly bulk as compliant for SLA reporting, provided the job is idempotent and traceable. We prefer to keep a Service Credit trigger if the job exceeds 12 hours.

2) Idempotency model: we support two safe patterns:
  - client-provided idempotency key (recommended): every job or logical transaction includes idempotency-id; Redwood persists dedupe keys for 36 hours by default (TTL configurable). Retries that present the same idempotency-id will be treated as no-op for duplicate application.
  - de-dupe on deterministic content hash: for legacy pipelines without stable keys we can compute a strong fingerprint; dedupe TTL 48 hours, higher compute cost.

3) Retry semantics and at-most-once: Redwood's runtime is naturally at-least-once at the transport layer for async batch; attaining application-level at-most-once requires idempotency keys (server-side enforcement) or transaction-level checkpoints. We'll enforce idempotency at write-time when keys exist. For your invoice use-case we recommend client-generated ids at ingest and a 48-hour dedupe window.

4) Safe-retry playbook (summary):
  - exponential backoff with jitter for transient 5xx and rate-limit 429.
  - max retry period: 6 hours for individual record attempts; overall job-level retries allowed within the 12-hour completion window.
  - failure-state reporting: any record that fails after N retries moves to a dead-letter set accessible via API, with payload and error codes.

5) Observability / proof: we can provide a per-job report (start/finish times, dedupe hits, retry counts) and an audit log extract for contract compliance.

6) Risk & controls: to accept the 12-hour carveout we should add a customer obligation paragraph: client must provide stable idempotency keys or agree to the dedupe-on-hash fallback with its limitations.

Elena —

Thanks for the request and patience. Based on engineering's input (below) here's a customer-facing summary we can include in the SOW and your operational runbook. Please review and tell me if you want stronger guarantees or different timing.

Draft SOW paragraph (suggested):
"Redwood will treat nightly bulk jobs for HyperLytics as compliant if job completion occurs within a 12-hour window from scheduled start, subject to the following conditions: (1) HyperLytics will supply a stable idempotency key per logical transaction at ingest; (2) Redwood will persist deduplication keys for 36 hours by default (configurable); (3) in the absence of client-provided keys, Redwood may compute deterministic content fingerprints with a 48-hour dedupe window; (4) retries will use exponential backoff with jitter and will not exceed 6 hours per-record; (5) audit logs and per-job reports will be provided to substantiate compliance. Service credits apply if completion exceeds 12 hours."

Operational notes (for your SREs):
- Use idempotency-id header: X-Idempotency-Key
- If you cannot provide stable ids, append deterministic-hash to payload and tag jobs with job-run-id
- Dead-letter records are accessible at /v1/jobs/{job-id}/deadletter with reasons and raw payloads

Next steps:
1) Confirm the SOW paragraph or suggest edits
2) Sign the waiver appendix (we'll send a short DocuSign)
3) We will provision a 36-hour dedupe TTL and provide an audit sample for the first 3 nightly runs

I've attached the technical draft for your ops team. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through the retry playbook.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
